results.question: what are our minions called?
results.reply:
Directly under you as Marshals are the Inspectors (*metsuke*, "one who directs their eye"), one assigned to each domain.
Under each Inspector are the Escorts (*gosonin*, "transport guard"), who form teams to bring in fugitives and claim bounties.
The full chain of command can be viewed on the [Wasp hierarchy](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/wasp-hierarchy) org chart.

results.question: Who is our boss?
results.reply:
Your boss is [Tsuruchi Kyoma](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-kyoma), the Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies of the Wasp. 

You and the other PCs serve as his yoriki (assistants), reporting to him a few times a week as Marshals (*haribugyo*) overseeing bounty hunting across the six southeastern domains.

results.question: who are the fortunes that the crab worship?
results.reply:
The Crab Clan's two patron Fortunes are:
Bishamon, the Fortune of strength.
Ebisu, the Fortune of honest work.

results.question: what are the imperial bounties?
results.reply:
Rewards registered with an Imperial magistrate for bringing in a fugitive or summoned witness.
By clan charter, every Wasp samurai may act as an Imperial magistrate to pursue them.
Payment goes to whoever registered it: half to the hunter, a tenth to their superior, and the rest to the daimyo's treasury.
The system is governed by the Doctrine of Three Steps.
The open wanted list is tracked on the [Imperial bulletin](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/imperial-bulletin), and the rules are detailed under [Imperial bounties](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/imperial-bounties).

results.question: what is the WASP org chart?
results.reply:
The chain of command for Wasp bounty hunting in the southeast is:
- [Tsuruchi Kyoma](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-kyoma), Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies
- Marshals (haribugyo; your PCs, upper 7th rank)
- Inspectors (metsuke, one per domain, lower 7th rank)
- Escorts (gosonin, small teams under each Inspector)
The full diagram is on the [Wasp hierarchy](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/wasp-hierarchy) page.

results.question: what's the word for the guys who haul fugitives back for the reward?
results.reply:
An **Escort** (*gosonin*, literally "transport guard"). 

They serve on an Inspector's (*metsuke*) team to help collect bounties and deliver the fugitive (or their head) to claim the reward. See the [Wasp hierarchy](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/wasp-hierarchy) for how they fit into the chain of command.

results.question: what's our title in Japanese?
results.reply: Your title as Wasp Marshals is **haribugyo** (meaning "magistrates of the sting").

results.question: what does metsuke mean?
results.reply: *Metsuke* means "one who directs their eye." In the Wasp hierarchy, it is the title for an Inspector (lower 7th rank), an officer assigned to oversee bounty hunting in one of the six domains under the Marshals.

results.question: what does haribugyo literally mean
results.reply: *Haribugyo* literally means "magistrates of the sting."

results.question: gosonin literally means what?
results.reply: *Gosonin* literally means "transport guard" (Escort).

results.question: what do people call the wasp chancellery?
results.reply:
The Wasp Clan chancellery is called [the Crane wives](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/the-crane-wives). 

It consists of three Crane courtiers married to [Tsuruchi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi) and his two top retainers:
- [Tsuruchi Naomi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-naomi) (Tsuruchi lineage)
- [Tsuruchi Ami](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-ami) (Ami lineage)
- [Tsuruchi Hitomi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-hitomi) (Kyoma lineage)

results.question: what's the name of the lineage for the wasp who used to be peasants?
results.reply:
The Wasp Clan's "peasantborn" lineage is the **Ami lineage**. 

It is made up mostly of the peasant yoriki and mercenaries who helped [Tsuruchi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi) and were raised to the samurai caste, and is headed on the chancellery by [Tsuruchi Ami](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-ami).

results.question: what are the sparrow samurai who live in the villages called?
results.reply:
They are called village overseers. 
They manage farming villages in place of peasant headsmen, sworn to a vow of poverty before the Fortune Daikoku.
You can read more about them on the [Sparrow Clan](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/sparrow-clan) page.

results.question: what's Kyoma's official title again
results.reply: [Tsuruchi Kyoma](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-kyoma)'s official title is Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies of the Wasp.

results.question: who reports to who in the wasp?
results.reply:
The chain of command for bounty operations in the southeast is:
- [Tsuruchi Kyoma](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-kyoma) (Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies)
- The Marshals (*haribugyo*, the PCs, upper 7th rank)
- One Inspector (*metsuke*, lower 7th rank) per domain
- Teams of Escorts (*gosonin*) under each Inspector

You can see the full org chart on the [Wasp hierarchy](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/wasp-hierarchy) page.

results.question: what's the wasp founder's saying, the single arrow thing?
results.reply:
The saying is "A single arrow, a single life." 

It was the motto of [Tsuruchi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi), first of his name, from his days as a bounty hunter, preferring to bring down fugitives with his bow rather than engage in duels.

results.question: what was the name of the sword tsuruchi broke?
results.reply: That sword was Isshin, the ancestral sword of the Shin lineage.

results.question: what does yoriki mean
results.reply:
*Yoriki* translates literally to "assistant." 

In Rokugan, it designates an assistant to a magistrate or other official; for example, the player character Marshals serve as yoriki to [Tsuruchi Kyoma](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-kyoma).

results.question: who is our inspector in the Reiji domain?
results.reply: Your Inspector (*metsuke*) in the Reiji domain is [Tsuruchi Fumitake](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-fumitake).

results.question: which inspector covers the sparrow lands
results.reply: [Tsuruchi Riku](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-riku) is the Wasp Inspector (*metsuke*) assigned to the Sparrow domain, based at Shiro Suzume.

results.question: who is the imperial magistrate for kakita lands?
results.reply: The Imperial magistrate for the Kakita domain is [Seppun Shogo](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/seppun-shogo), stationed at Kyuden Kakita.

results.question: who runs the fox clan
results.reply: The Fox Clan is led by its daimyo, [Kitsune Ryosei](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/kitsune-ryosei).

results.question: who's the sparrow daimyo?
results.reply: The daimyo of the Sparrow Clan is [Suzume Mukashino](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/suzume-mukashino).

results.question: who founded the wasp clan
results.reply: The Wasp Clan was founded by [Tsuruchi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi), first of his name (born Bayushi no Kyo Tsuruchi of the Shin lineage), about 15 years ago with Crane backing.

results.question: who is the imperial chancellor
results.reply:
The Imperial Chancellor is Kakita Yoshi. 

A Crane of the 14th rank, he heads the Imperial chancellery, showed [Tsuruchi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi) his uncle's treacherous correspondence, promised Crane support, and arranged the charter that created the Wasp Clan.

results.question: who runs kyomas house in sparrow lands?
results.reply: [Tsuruchi Kyoma](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-kyoma)'s residence in Shiro Suzume is run by his household steward, [Tsuruchi Byakuya](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-byakuya), an old friend from the Kyo house.

results.question: who's the superstitious lady who gave us the anti-fox charms?
results.reply:
You are thinking of [Tsuruchi Tatsuki](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-tatsuki), though he is actually male. 
He is the household steward of [Tsuruchi Kyoma](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-kyoma)'s Fox Clan residence in Shinden Kitsune. 
Deeply superstitious, he gave you amulets and charms against fox mischief for entering the Kitsune Mori.

results.question: what's Kyoma's wife's name
results.reply:
[Tsuruchi Kyoma](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-kyoma)'s wife is [Tsuruchi Hitomi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-hitomi). 

She was born a Kakita and is one of the "Crane wives" on the Wasp Clan chancellery, serving as the head of the Kyoma lineage.

results.question: who is the wasp daimyo's wife?
results.reply: The Wasp Clan daimyo [Tsuruchi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi) is married to [Tsuruchi Naomi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-naomi). She is the youngest daughter of the Crane Clan Champion Doji Kuwanen, one of "the Crane wives," and heads the Wasp's Tsuruchi lineage.

results.question: who had our job before us?
results.reply:
You replaced the three previous Marshals (*haribugyo*):
- [Tsuruchi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi) Kaminari
- Tsuruchi Danji
- Tsuruchi Okihito
All three were promoted in 1130 to serve as Marshals in the Yasuki Estates.

results.question: who is Hideki?
results.reply:
[Tsuruchi Hideki](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-hideki) is a Wasp Escort (*gosonin*) of the Ami lineage.
He is stationed in Shiro Reiji, serving on the team of the domain's Inspector, [Tsuruchi Fumitake](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-fumitake).

results.question: who is seppun gorou
results.reply: [Seppun Gorou](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/seppun-gorou) is the Imperial magistrate posted to the Fox Clan domain, residing in its capital of Shinden Kitsune.

results.question: who's coming after us for the teahouse thing?
results.reply:
The family of [Ikoma Tsai](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-tsai), the Ikoma shugenja killed at the teahouse during the [Family Reckoning](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/the-family-reckoning):
- [Ikoma Wataemon](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-wataemon), his father (Provincial Minister of Rites for the Ikoma Family)
- [Ikoma Naohira](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-naohira), his brother (Deputy Provincial Minister of War)
- [Ikoma Ietsugu](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-ietsugu), his brother (an Ikoma priest)
They have declared a lawful [blood feud](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/blood-feuds) against the Wasp present and their kin, and are traveling south.

results.question: who did the hermit attack?
results.reply: [Shoda](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/shoda) the hermit attacked the county magistrate [Bayushi no Daika Koharu](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/bayushi-no-daika-koharu) from behind with an axe in the Kitsune forest, accusing him of hunting foxes.

results.question: which domains do we cover?
results.reply:
As Wasp Marshals, you oversee bounty hunting across six domains:
• Fox domain (Kitsune lands; capital Shinden Kitsune)
• Sparrow domain (Suzume lands; capital Shiro Suzume)
• Kakita domain (Crane lands; capital Kyuden Kakita)
• Etsuko domain (Daidoji lands; capital Shiro Etsuko)
• Reiji domain (Hida lands; capital Shiro Reiji)
• Daika domain (Bayushi lands; capital Shiro Daika)

results.question: which of our domains are crane?
results.reply:
Two of the six domains you oversee are Crane lands:

- **Kakita domain**: the ruling house of the Kakita Family of the Crane Clan (capital Kyuden Kakita).
- **Etsuko domain**: the northernmost Daidoji domain of the Crane Clan (capital Shiro Etsuko).

results.question: what province does the wasp clan hold?
results.reply: The Wasp Clan's entire territory is the mountainous Hachinaga province, which guards the Hachinaga pass through the Spine of the World Mountains.

results.question: what's the alliance of the three little clans called?
results.reply:
It is called the [Three Man Alliance](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/three-man-alliance) (also referred to as the southern allies). 

The three member clans are:
- Wasp Clan (leading the alliance)
- Fox Clan
- Sparrow Clan

results.question: who's in the three man alliance?
results.reply:
The Three Man Alliance consists of three minor clans of the southeast:
- The Wasp Clan (Tsuruchi Family), at its head
- The Fox Clan (Kitsune Family)
- The Sparrow Clan (Suzume Family)

For more details on the pact, see the [Three Man Alliance](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/three-man-alliance) page.

results.question: what's the big fox forest called?
results.reply: It is called the **Kitsune Mori** ("fox forest").

results.question: what does the ministry of retainers do?
results.reply:
The Ministry of Retainers is responsible for samurai stipends, ranks, civil service exams, and promotions. 
At the Imperial level, it also awards honors and commendations (such as the Order of the Precious Crown).

results.question: which ministry pays samurai their stipends?
results.reply: The Ministry of Retainers is responsible for samurai stipends, ranks, civil service exams, and promotions.

results.question: what is the emerald champion?
results.reply:
The Emerald Champion is the title of the Imperial Minister of Justice, one of the Six Ministries.
The post is chosen by a dueling tournament to determine the best duelist in the Empire, who duels on the Emperor's behalf.
The office oversees policing, bandit patrols, courts, jails, and Imperial magistrates across Rokugan.

results.question: what is the shogun?
results.reply:
The **Shogun** is the title of the Imperial Minister of War, one of the Six Ministries. 

They oversee the Imperial Legions as well as the Empire's armies, weapons, armor, horses, and maps.

results.question: what rank are we?
results.reply:
As Wasp Marshals (*haribugyo*), you and your fellow PCs are of the upper 7th rank (7.5). 

Under the Doctrine of Three Steps, that places you just above the domain Inspectors (*metsuke*), who hold the lower 7th rank.

results.question: what rank is a county magistrate?
results.reply: A County Magistrate is of rank 5 in the samurai caste hierarchy.

results.question: what is the doctrine of three steps
results.reply:
The [Doctrine of Three Steps](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/doctrine-of-three-steps) governs the Measure of Standing between samurai of different ranks for bounties, duels, and arrests.
- Samurai within three formal ranks of each other are of accordant standing (required to interview someone or share a small table); beyond three, they are discordant.
- Samurai within one rank of each other, adjusted for merits under the "totality of circumstance", are of peer standing.
- Peer standing is required to arrest a samurai.
- A duel challenge may be dismissed if the challenger is more than three formal ranks below the challenged ("beyond the reach").

results.question: how far does a blood feud reach?
results.reply:
A blood feud extends to every descendant of each named person's paternal great-grandfather on both sides.
Anyone included under this lineage may lawfully kill anyone on the other side.
Outsiders gain nothing from participating in the feud.
More details are on the [blood feuds](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/blood-feuds) page.

results.question: what was the family reckoning?
results.reply:
The Family Reckoning was a messy, all-hands Wasp bounty mission to deliver an Imperial summons to [Ikoma Yuan](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-yuan) at a teahouse. 

The job went wrong and the Ikoma shugenja [Ikoma Tsai](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-tsai) was killed. 

His father [Ikoma Wataemon](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-wataemon) and brothers [Ikoma Naohira](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-naohira) and [Ikoma Ietsugu](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/ikoma-ietsugu) declared a lawful blood feud against the Wasp present, which extends to their relatives (including the PCs). The three Ikoma are currently traveling south to pursue it.

The wiki overview of the incident is at [the Family Reckoning](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/the-family-reckoning).

results.question: what does righteous sting mean?
results.reply:
Righteous Sting is a custom advantage tied to the mess at the teahouse during the Family Reckoning.
It means your relative at the teahouse acted honorably during that confrontation.
Mechanically, it causes your Rank to count higher, and raises the party's effective Rank as well.
The rules for it are detailed on the [custom advantages and disadvantages](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/custom-advantages-and-disadvantages) page.

results.question: what does the peasantborn disadvantage do
results.reply:
You are the child of a peasant [Tsuruchi](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi) raised to the samurai caste. 
As a result, you are never considered to be of peer standing with samurai-born individuals. 
More details are on the [custom advantages and disadvantages](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/custom-advantages-and-disadvantages) page.

results.question: how much of a bounty do we keep?
results.reply:
Traditionally, the bounty hunter keeps half (50%) of the collected reward. 

Your superior takes a tenth (10%), and the remaining forty percent (40%) goes to the daimyo's treasury.

results.question: who is the fortune of honest work
results.reply:
Ebisu is the Fortune of honest work, one of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck.
He is a patron Fortune of the Crab Clan and Dragon Clan.

results.question: what's the love fortune called
results.reply:
Benten is the Fortune of romantic love, one of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck.
She is a patron Fortune of both the Crane Clan and the Scorpion Clan.

results.question: what fortunes do the dragon pray to
results.reply:
The patron Fortunes of the Dragon Clan are:
- Hotei (Fortune of contentment)
- Ebisu (Fortune of honest work)

results.question: what are my old clan's patron fortunes?
results.reply:
The Lion Clan's two patron Fortunes are:
- Bishamon, Fortune of strength
- Daikoku, Fortune of wealth

results.question: which temples would my birth clan build in every city?
results.reply:
Your birth clan, the Crab Clan, has two patron Fortunes, building a temple to each in every city:
A temple to Bishamon, Fortune of strength
A temple to Ebisu, Fortune of honest work

results.question: which fortune is the fox and rice one
results.reply: That is Inari, the Fortune of rice and of foxes.

results.question: what clan was I originally from?
results.reply: You were originally from the Phoenix Clan (Asako Family), trained in the Isawa Ishi school, before joining the Wasp Clan.

results.question: what clan did I come from?
results.reply: You originally came from the Scorpion Clan (trained at the Yogo Warden school, in the Tsuruchi lineage of former Scorpion).

results.question: what school am I?
results.reply: You are trained in the Mantis Wave-Treader school (at 3rd Dan).

results.question: is there a bounty on me?
results.reply:
Yes, there is an open [Imperial bulletin](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/imperial-bulletin) bounty on you for 50 koku.
It was posted after you accepted a duel challenge from Bayushi no Daika Isoshi and then left to "meditate."
The Fox Clan daimyo, [Kitsune Ryosei](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/kitsune-ryosei), has refused to compel your return.

results.question: who was the guy on the bulletin with the goiter?
results.reply:
That is [Shoda](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/shoda) the hermit, an old hermit with long gray hair and a goiter on the right of his neck.
He attacked [Bayushi no Daika Koharu](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/bayushi-no-daika-koharu) with an axe in the Kitsune forest for hunting foxes.
He carries a 100 koku bounty on the [Imperial bulletin](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/imperial-bulletin).

results.question: which bounty is the opium smuggler
results.reply:
Hiruma Kojiro (100 koku bounty): he runs an Empire-wide opium cartel, travels with Yasuki caravans, and avoids boats for fear of Osano-Wo.
Open bounties are tracked on the [Imperial bulletin](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/imperial-bulletin).

results.question: the bandits that wait in the river ford, what are they called?
results.reply: They are the heron bandits, a gang of tall, thin bandits who rob travelers mid-ford in the Mugi-arai-gawa between Fox and Daidoji lands. They carry an open bounty of 30 koku on the [Imperial bulletin](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/imperial-bulletin).

results.question: who's the fake charcoal guy
results.reply:
"Kitsune Denhei" is the fake name used by an unidentified target selling counterfeit Fox Clan white charcoal in Kakita and Etsuko lands.
There is an open [Imperial bulletin](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/imperial-bulletin) bounty of 40 koku to discover their real identity.

results.question: list of open bounties?
results.reply:
Open bounties are tracked on the [Imperial bulletin](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/wikis/imperial-bulletin):
• 100 koku: Hiruma Kojiro, Shione Budi, [Shoda](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/shoda) the hermit, the many-colored Yasuki, the oxbow river gang
• 75 koku: Kage the shadow-bandit, Shinjiro the obsidian merchant, Recovery of the Singing Branch

• 40-15 koku: The stuttering bandit gang (40), Kitsune Denhei (40), the heron bandits (30), The Fox Road footpads (25), Roku the porter (20), the tide-trap gang (20), Doji no Tsume Hariya (20), [Bayushi no Daika Rentaro](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/bayushi-no-daika-rentaro) (15), Iwao the ashigaru (15)
• 10-5 koku: Saburo three-towns (10), the red-ear fugitive (10), Genichi the gambler (5)

results.question: what's the bear that never found a den called
results.reply:
It is called an **anamotazu** ("the one with no den"). 
It is a moon bear of the Kitsune Mori that never denned and hunts hungry through the winter.

results.question: which of tatsukis amulets was the bell
results.reply:
It is the pilgrim's bell (junrei-suzu). 

Given to the Marshals by [Tsuruchi Tatsuki](https://waspbountyhunters.obsidianportal.com/characters/tsuruchi-tatsuki) for entering the Kitsune Mori, it is a small brass bell carried on a staff or pack that prevents fox-illusions from easily replacing the path behind you while it rings.

results.question: what does TN stand for
results.reply: TN stands for Target Number: the value a roll must meet or exceed to succeed.

results.question: what's the difference between rolled and kept dice?
results.reply:
A roll is written as **XkY**:
- **Rolled dice (X)** are the total number of ten-sided dice you roll, equal to your skill plus the relevant Ring.
- **Kept dice (Y)** are how many of the highest dice you keep and add together for your total, equal to your Ring.
- Any 10 rolled explodes (reroll it and add the result).
- No roll exceeds 10 dice: extra rolled dice become kept dice, and extra kept dice beyond 10k10 add a flat +1 each.

results.question: what does a feint do?
results.reply:
A feint is a Fire school knack attack roll made in place of the attack skill.
It deals no damage, but on a success it grants a temporary void point.
Additionally, your highest action die is moved to the current combat phase.

results.question: how many void points can i spend on a roll?
results.reply:
You may spend no more void points on a single roll than your lowest Ring.
Each void point spent allows you to roll and keep one extra die (+1k1).
Void points cannot be spent on damage rolls.

results.question: how is my dan determined?
results.reply: Your Dan (level of school mastery, First through Fifth) equals the rank of your lowest school knack. Each Dan grants you access to one of your school's techniques.

results.question: how much is a free raise worth
results.reply: A free raise provides a +5 bonus to a roll's total.

results.question: when am i impaired
results.reply:
You become impaired when your current number of serious wounds equals your Earth Ring.
While impaired, your 10s on skill rolls do not explode (no rerolled 10s).

results.question: when is the festival where the ancestors come back
results.reply: That is Obon (the Bon Festival). It takes place on the 15th day of the 7th month (the Month of the Rooster), when ancestors' spirits are invited home for a day and a night of masked dancing under lanterns.

results.question: what was the day of thunder?
results.reply:
The Day of Thunder was a cataclysmic coup in 1123 led by a cult of Lord Moon (Onnotangu). 

The cult murdered Scorpion daimyo Bayushi Shoju, and Grand Abbot Okawa gathered the Seven Thunders to confront them. 

The Thunders defeated the moon cultist Shinjo Jotsu, but the bloodspeaker Jama no Iuchiban Kohaku slew the surviving Thunders. 

Following the catastrophe, praying to Lord Moon inside a temple consecrated to Lady Sun (Amaterasu) was declared heresy.

results.question: how many bu in a koku
results.reply: There are 10 silver bu to one gold koku (1 koku = 10 bu = 100 zeni = 1,000 sen).

results.question: what time is the hour of the rat
results.reply: The Hour of the Rat is midnight to 2am.

results.question: who was shinjo jotsu
results.reply:
Shinjo Jotsu was an Imperial magistrate secretly heir to the moon cult.
He had the prophet Baiten murdered.
He served on the Imperial Board of Justice during the occupation of Toshi Ranbo (from the First Toshi Ranbo campaign).
He was supplied with obsidian by the bounty target Shinjiro the obsidian merchant.
He was ultimately defeated by the Seven Thunders on the Day of Thunder in 1123.

results.question: who writes the rules for imperial magistrates
results.reply:
Their duties are defined by the Emerald Charter, under the Ministry of Justice headed by the Emerald Champion.
Historically, the Fortune Saibankan (in life Soshi Saibankan) wrote the Emerald Charter and established Rokugan's common law of precedent.

results.question: why do people avoid the number four
results.reply:
The number four sounds like "death" (shi), so Rokugani consider it unlucky and actively avoid it.
They avoid taking journeys on the 4th, do not build four-story buildings, and add a coin to gifts of four coins.
Giving someone four of an item is taken as an explicit threat.
